description: Ozero Mail: one calm inbox for Gmail, iCloud, Exchange and any IMAP mail (Outlook soon), with shared folders and people first. No AI, no ads, no tracking.
h1: All your email. One calm inbox.
sub: I’m making the email app I couldn’t find for myself. For Android and iPhone, no AI.

pains.a: The inbox is a to-do list, not an archive. Done moves a letter to the archive, nothing is deleted. Snooze brings it back when you need it. The bar at the bottom shows what’s left, and at zero it goes quiet. Try it here: swipe this letter left.

pains.q: One inbox, but five Sent folders?
pains.a: Most apps merge only the inbox. Here Sent, Archive, Spam and Trash are shared across accounts too, like in Apple Mail. Gmail, iCloud, Exchange at work or any IMAP mail; Outlook is coming.
Your company’s Exchange sits next to your own mail; the address and password are enough. An invitation comes as a card: answer right in the letter, and the day strip shows what it clashes with.
Only you and your mail provider. No AI, no ads, no tracking. Images in newsletters stay hidden, so senders can’t tell you opened them.

pains.q: Real letters lost in the noise?
pains.a: People get the inbox. Newsletters and notifications wait in their own tabs, sorted by simple rules on your phone. You can leave a newsletter right from a letter.
Me, Khizri. I design and build it alone, for my own inbox. Mail is free forever; extras are a one-time purchase. You pay me, not a corporation. No ads, ever.

privacy.title: Privacy · Ozero Mail
privacy.lead: Ozero Mail is made by one person, Khizri Makhmudov. This page says what the app and this site do with your data. In short: your mail stays between your phone and your mail provider. I never see it.

p: The app connects straight from your phone to your mail provider: Gmail, your company’s Exchange server, or any server that speaks IMAP and SMTP. Messages, addresses and settings are stored only on your phone, in an encrypted database.
None of it passes through a server of mine. I have no copy and no way to read it.

For Gmail, you sign in on Google’s own page, and the app gets a key to your mailbox. For other mailboxes, Exchange included, you give the app your password, and a certificate if your company asks for one. All of it is kept on your phone, sealed with a key that never leaves the phone’s secure storage.
Removing an account in the app deletes its mail and its key from the phone. Removing the app deletes everything, including the list of senders whose images you allowed.
With your permission, the app reads, sends and organizes your Gmail. It does this only to show your mail, send what you write and carry out what you do, such as archiving or marking as read.

Ozero Mail’s use and transfer to any other app of information received from Google APIs will adhere to the [Google API Services User Data Policy](https://developers.google.com/terms/api-services-user-data-policy), including the Limited Use requirements. Your Gmail data is not passed to anyone, not used for ads and not used to train AI models. I do not read it, unless you send me a letter yourself.
You can take the access back at any time in your [Google Account](https://myaccount.google.com/permissions).
Your answer to an invitation goes from your own mailbox, or straight to your Exchange server. The day strip next to it is built from invitations in your mail.
Add to calendar opens your phone’s calendar with the meeting filled in. The app does not read your calendar.
Senders often hide tiny images in letters to learn when you open them. The app holds remote images back, so they learn nothing.

Images load for letters from people and from senders you allowed. Tapping Show loads them and allows that sender from now on. Then the phone downloads the images from the sender’s server, which sees your IP address, as with any download. Images in junk never load.
The app has no analytics, no ads and no third-party code that collects data. It sends nothing to me.

sections.h: Crash reports and letters to me
p: If the app crashes, it keeps a short report on your phone and asks next time whether to send it. If you agree, it opens an ordinary letter from your own mailbox to me, and you can read it before sending. The report says where in the code the app failed, the app and system versions and the phone’s maker and model. It holds no mail. Like any letter, it shows me your address and name.
I use your letters only to answer you and to fix the app. Ask, and I will delete them.

This site sets no cookies and loads nothing from other services; even the fonts come from here. The host, Netlify, keeps ordinary server logs (IP address, page and time) to deliver and protect the site.
The “Write to me” button opens your own mail app. The site stores nothing.
If anything here changes, I will update this page and its date, and say so in the app’s release notes.

privacy.description: What Ozero Mail and its site do with your data: your mail stays between your phone and your mail provider.
